svg.text: SOLAR COLD CHAIN SITE — REPRESENTATIVE SINGLE LINE & PROCESS DIAGRAM
Health-facility and agricultural cold chain: ~12 kWp PV · ~50 kWh battery · direct-drive and AC refrigeration
A 30-day temperature logger sits in every appliance
Walk-in cold room: 10 to 14 h above 0 °C with the doors kept shut
Ice-lined refrigerator: 3 days holding +2 to +8 °C with no power
Ice bank: one full night of cold room running without the genset
Battery: one night plus one cloudy day of base load
Size every unit for the worst month, not the annual average
product path and holding temperature — the power system above exists to hold these bands
Direct-drive appliances run straight off the array and store the solar peak as ice inside the appliance.
That buys several days of holdover in cloudy weather without cycling the battery at all.
Sizing is driven by holdover hours, not daily energy: every unit must ride through the night unattended.
An ice bank is usually cheaper per hour of holdover than the equivalent extra battery capacity.
Compressor starting current sets the inverter rating — allow three to five times the running power.
Vaccine appliances should be WHO PQS prequalified and keep a 30-day electronic temperature record.
